Local Court of the Northern Territory
note: Verified against legislation.nt.gov.au on 2026-08-26. The Supreme Court Rules 1987 carry their own time code in O 3 r 3.01: the start day is excluded and the end day included, periods of 5 days or less skip days the Registry is closed, and a last day on which the Registry is closed moves to the next day it is open; the Registry is open every day except Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays under the Public Holidays Act 1981 (r 3.07(1)). Interpretation Act 1978 s 28 applies to statutory instruments through s 4 and produces the same result (exclusive of the trigger day; last day on a Saturday, Sunday or whole-day public holiday moves to the next day that is none of those) and is tabled as a secondary provision. The script approximates registry-open days with the weekend-and-public-holiday table (Darwin basis), and every computed date carries a warning to confirm the registry was open. Local Court (Civil Jurisdiction) Rules periods are not tabled here. An entry returned to pending-verification fails closed until re-verified.

computation_provisions.summary: Calculating time: a period fixed by Chapter 1, by a judgment or order, or by a document in a proceeding is calculated under r 3.01 (r 3.01(1)); where a period of one day or longer is to begin on or be calculated from a day or event, that day is excluded (r 3.01(2)); where it is to end on or be calculated to a day or event, that day is included (r 3.01(3)); where a period of 5 days or less would include a day on which the Registry is closed, that day is excluded (r 3.01(4)); where the last day for doing an act at the Registry is a day on which the Registry is closed, the act may be done on the next day the Registry is open (r 3.01(5)). The Registry is open every day except Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays under the Public Holidays Act 1981 (r 3.07(1)), from 9.00 am to 4.00 pm unless the Chief Justice directs otherwise (r 3.07(2)). Extension and abridgment sit in r 3.02.

computation_provisions.summary: Reckoning of time: a period dating from a given day, act or event is reckoned exclusive of that day (s 28(1)); a period expressed to end at, with or on a given day includes that day (s 28(1A)); if the last day of a period for doing a thing falls on a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the place where the thing is to be done (other than a part-day public holiday), the thing may be done on the first following day that is none of those (s 28(2)). The Act applies to statutory instruments made under laws to which it applies as if they were Acts (s 4). The dictionary 'business day' likewise excludes Saturdays, Sundays and whole-day public holidays in the relevant place.

period_rules.label: Notice of appearance after service of writ (Darwin Registry, service within 200 km of Darwin)
period_rules.trigger: Service of the writ or originating motion on the defendant within the Territory, within 200 kilometres of Darwin, for process filed in the Darwin Registry
warnings: Rule 8.04 fixes the minimum time the writ must state ('not less than 7 days after service'); the operative deadline is the time stated in the writ, which may be longer, and the Court may otherwise order — check the writ. The computed date is the earliest the rule permits, not necessarily the date on the writ.

Other limbs are not computed: service within 200 km of Alice Springs for process filed there is also 7 days (r 8.04(a)(ii)); service in the Territory more than 200 km from the filing Registry is 14 days (r 8.04(a)(iii)); service elsewhere in Australia is 21 days (r 8.04(b)); New Zealand or Papua New Guinea 28 days (r 8.04(c)); any other case 42 days (r 8.04(d)).
An appearance is filed in the Registry in which the originating process was filed and a sealed copy served on the plaintiff the same or the next working day (r 8.05(1)).

Rollover is computed as the next weekday that is not a listed NT public holiday (Darwin basis); r 3.01(5) turns on days the Registry is closed (r 3.07) — confirm the registry was open on the candidate date and use the Alice Springs show day for the Alice Springs Registry.

evidence.method: Plain HTTP download of the official current consolidation PDF, text extracted with pdftotext; r 8.04 read in full and the 7-day limb confirmed exactly, r 8.05 read for the warnings.

period_rules.label: Defence after service of a separate statement of claim
period_rules.trigger: Service of the plaintiff's statement of claim on a defendant who has filed an appearance (proceeding commenced by writ)
warnings: Where the endorsement of claim on the writ itself constitutes a statement of claim under r 5.04, the defence is instead due within 14 days after filing the appearance (r 14.04(a)) — supply the appearance-filing date as the trigger if that limb applies; the Court may also direct a different time (r 14.04(c)).
The rule requires service of the defence within the period; filing is governed by r 14.10 — confirm both steps.

Rollover is computed as the next weekday that is not a listed NT public holiday (Darwin basis); r 3.01(5) turns on days the Registry is closed (r 3.07) — confirm the registry was open on the candidate date.

evidence.method: Plain HTTP download of the official current consolidation PDF, text extracted with pdftotext; r 14.04 read in full and the 14-day limb confirmed exactly.
evidence.version: Supreme Court Rules 1987, as in force at 23 June 2025

period_rules.label: Notice of appeal (Court of Appeal or Full Court) where no Act fixes the period
period_rules.trigger: The day the decision being appealed from is made; the period runs after that day
warnings: The 28 days apply only if no period is required for commencing the appeal under an Act (r 82.04(2)(a)-(b)); where the enabling Act fixes a period, that period governs and is not computed here — check the Supreme Court Act 1979 and any statute conferring the right of appeal.

Chapter 2 (O 82) applies to all appeals under a Territory law to the Supreme Court as a single judge or Full Court, as the Court of Appeal under Part III of the Supreme Court Act, and as the Court of Criminal Appeal (r 82.02); the notice must be both filed and served within the period (r 82.04(2)). Applications for leave or to extend time follow O 82 Part 3.

Rule 3.01 governs periods fixed by Chapter 1; for this Chapter 2 period the same computation applies through r 82.03 (the definitions and rules in Chapter 1 apply to any matter respecting an appeal not otherwise provided for, with the necessary changes) and, independently, Interpretation Act s 28.

Rollover is computed as the next weekday that is not a listed NT public holiday (Darwin basis); r 3.01(5) turns on days the Registry is closed (r 3.07) — confirm the registry was open on the candidate date.
